titleStmt.title: Safeguards in Provision of German Units

head.hi: Safeguards in Provision of German Units

list.label: (a)
list.item: German units would at no time be under the authority and command of the German Federal Republic;
list.label: (b)
(c)
list.item: Under this arrangement there need be no general staff as such in Germany but merely an administrative and logistical agency.

list.label: (a)
list.item: The maximum number of German units can be controlled by NATO. This could be done by fixing (1) an arbitrary maximum number, or sliding scale increase schedule; (2) an arbitrary ratio of the number of German units in comparison with Allied Divisions available for the defense of Western Europe. If the French wish, it might be possible to arrive in addition at a satisfactory proportion between German and French units;
list.label: (b)
list.item: As a practical matter, German units will start out far behind French units and always remain in lesser proportion. The fact that there are no preparations in Germany, and the equipment problem itself, makes this a practical fact;
list.label: (c)
list.item:
The head of the Federal Agency in Germany could be a carefully selected
                        civilian and steps could be taken to insure the democratic 
 implementation of such limited prerogatives
                        as the Germans would have in the defense field;
list.label: (d)
list.item: The Occupying Powers would retain general supervision over officer recruitment and be extremely careful about reliance upon Germany’s old officer class. A great deal could be done now to influence the future German officer corps;
list.label: (e)
list.item: There would remain Prohibited and Limited Industries in Germany and a Military Security Board to exercise continued military control. Certain changes in these agreements would be necessary but Germany would be restricted to the contribution of ground units and prohibited from making vital military equipment.

div.p: The above and perhaps additional safeguards can be obtained if we act now. As time proceeds, it is a certainty that Germany would demand more and more a status of full equality in connection with the provision armed units. There is today in Germany a spirit for European integration which has been greatly aided by the efforts of the French. We desire to take advantage of this situa[tion …].

note.p: Parts of several lines are missing from the source text.
